🏙️ City Walk

Rebuilds the streets, buildings, trees and parks around any UK postcode (or lat,lon) from OpenStreetMap, then lets you walk or drive as far as you like — the map streams in as you go.

📶 Uses mobile data: roughly 5–10 MB to start (more on High/Ultra graphics), then about 1–2 MB per km you drive or fly. Places you've visited are saved on your device, so coming back is almost free. Wi-Fi recommended.

Credits & licences

This is a free, non-commercial hobby project. It is built entirely from open data, downloaded live by your browser:

  • Streets, buildings, land use, bus stops, shops, house numbers — © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Served as vector tiles by OpenFreeMap (schema © OpenMapTiles), or live from the Overpass API in Full detail mode.
  • Ground heights (1 m) — Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM, © Environment Agency copyright and/or database right, Open Government Licence v3.
  • Ground heights (wider area & horizon) — Terrain Tiles (Mapzen / AWS Open Data; sources listed there).
  • Place search — postcodes.io (Contains OS data © Crown copyright, Royal Mail data © Royal Mail, ONS data © Crown copyright) and Nominatim (search only when you press Go, per its usage policy).
  • Listed buildings — National Heritage List for England, © Historic England, Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right, Open Government Licence v3. Used to find and name listed buildings; their 3D detail (towers, stonework, windows) is made up to suit, not surveyed.
  • Ward, council & region names — postcodes.io (Contains OS data © Crown copyright, ONS data © Crown copyright), looked up every few hundred metres as you travel. Neighbourhood and village names come with the OpenStreetMap data.
  • Live weather — Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0 (free API, non-commercial use).
  • Stars — HYG Database by David Nash, CC BY-SA 4.0, via d3-celestial © 2015 Olaf Frohn (BSD 3-Clause). The star table embedded in this page is shared under the same CC BY-SA 4.0 licence.
  • Planets — approximate orbital elements from NASA JPL (E. M. Standish). Sun & moon — standard low-precision astronomical formulae.
  • 3D engine — three.js (MIT); GeoTIFF reading — geotiff.js (MIT).

Anything not listed (house colours, windows, trees in parks, traffic, people, sounds) is generated by the app and isn't real data.
